source_title: Indian sports wrap, October 30: Anurag Thakur, Kiren Rijiju flag off Armwrestling championship - Sportstar
source_excerpt: CHENNAI MORE SPORTS Anurag Thakur, Kiren Rijiju open 47th World Armwrestling Championship in Delhi The 47th World Armwrestling and 28th World Para Armwrestling Championship 2026 were inaugurated in New Delhi on Thursday, October 29. Union minister Kiren Rijiju and former sports minister Anurag Singh Thakur attended, along with World Armwrestling Federation president Assen Hadjitodorov. Hosted in India for the first time by the People’s Armwrestling Federation of India, led by Preeti Jhangiani and Parvinn Dabass, the event has drawn over 1,700 athletes, officials and supporters from more than 60 countries. The ceremony featured Kerala drummers, a Parade of Nations and a lamp-lighting, followed by a 20-minute exhibition match between Pro Panja League athletes Prasenjeet Patra and Amit Singh. Rijiju congratulated the organisers on bringing the championship to India. The event runs until November 7. -Team Sportstar TENNIS Rohan Bopanna Tennis Academy partners with Hygiia Ventures to support young players Hygiia Ventures, which owns the Gurgaon Grand Slammers franchise in the Tennis Premier League (TPL), has partnered with the Rohan Bopanna Tennis Academy (RBTA) to support the development of young Indian tennis players. The partnership will focus on coaching, training, education, infrastructure, equipment, technology and tournament participation, while strengthening the academy’s high-performance programmes. Led by Gaurav Agarwal, Hygiia Ventures has been involved in Indian tennis through its ownership of the Gurgaon Grand Slammers. The association with RBTA will extend its involvement to grassroots and junior player development. Based at the Centre for Sports Excellence in Bengaluru, the academy supports players at different stages of their careers, including Vaishnavi Adkar, Sumit Nagal and Dhakshineswar Suresh. Through its Bhoomi Programme, RBTA also provides education, accommodation and tennis training to underprivileged children from Assam and Jammu. Bopanna said developing young athletes required consistent coaching, education and an environment that allowed them to improve over time. He welcomed the partnership, saying the additional support would help strengthen the academy’s training structure and provide more opportunities for aspiring players. Agarwal praised Bopanna’s contribution to Indian tennis and said both organisations shared a commitment to developing the country’s next generation of players. The academy, founded by the former World No. 1 doubles player, combines tennis coaching with sports science, fitness, recovery and competition support. The collaboration aims to provide young athletes with the resources and guidance needed to progress from junior competitions towards professional tennis. - Team Sportstar BOXING Commonwealth champion Arundhati alongside Aarti, Ankushita and Hussam power India to perfect start in Tampere Four Indian boxers advanced to the semifinals at the 46th International Tammer tournament with impressive wins on the opening day of competition in Tampere, Finland, while two more bouts featuring Jaismine and Hitesh are scheduled later today in Session 2. Commonwealth Games gold medallist Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) led the charge with a dominant win over Finland’s Vilma Kuusikko, while Aarti Dhariyal (54kg) registered a commanding victory against Sweden’s Britta Lia Tisell and Ankushita Boro (65kg) overcame Brazil’s Haziel Santos to move into the last four. In the men’s 60kg category, Hussam Uddin Mohammed produced a technically superior display to beat Scotland’s Luca Flynn and secure his semifinal berth. Later today, World Champion Jaismine (57kg) will open her campaign against Brazil’s Jessica Dias Coutinho, while Hitesh (70kg) will take on England’s Kyle Shaw-Tullin. -Team Sportstar FENCING 8th ISSO National Fencing Championship concludes at Shiv Nadar School, Faridabad Over 44 Schools Nationwide Compete in Thrilling Exhibition of Precision, Technique, and Swordsmanship The International Schools Sports Organisation (ISSO) successfully hosted the 8th ISSO National Fencing Championship (2026–27) at Shiv Nadar School, Faridabad. The premier two-day national event witnessed enthusiastic participation from 44 schools across the country, featuring young fencers competing across Under-14 (Sub-Junior), Under-17 (Cadet), and Under-19 age categories for both boys and girls across Sabre, Foil, and Épée disciplines. The championship showcased extraordinary tactical precision, athletic speed, and sportsmanship, providing a national platform for emerging school-level fencers. Patil International School, Nerul); 2nd – Deb Barma Ansh (Amity Global School, Gurgaon). -Team Sportstar BASKETBALL Youth Nationals: Teams book quarterfinal berths as league phase reaches home stretch Powerhouse teams tightened their grip as the quarterfinal contenders became clearer with just one day of league matches remaining at the CM Chashak 41st Youth National Basketball Championship. In the women’s section, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh have confirmed their berths in the knockout stage. Meanwhile, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Madhya Pradesh secured their quarterfinal spots in the men’s category after a day of intense action at the Chondhe Patil Sports Complex in Pune. In Level 2 action, Uttarakhand, Karnataka, Chandigarh, and Chhattisgarh topped their respective pools in the boys’ section, while Haryana, Chandigarh, Puducherry, and Jharkhand emerged as the pool leaders among the girls.
